24-hour priority list

You answer 3 of 4 questions in each part, so each part has its own list. Study down both lists until the green pass line: about 3 h for Part A and 3 h for Part B, which leaves time for sleep and a last read of the one-shot notes. Alternate between parts (A block 1, B block 1, A block 2 …) so neither is left short. Chance: how often the topic came up, newer papers weigh more (2023 ×6, 2022B ×5, 2022 ×5, 2021 ×3, 2020 ×2, 2019 ×1). Covered: share of that part's past-paper marks you have studied once you finish the row.

Retake tip: read the Concept Primer first (30 minutes). This course is almost all theory with diagrams, and the same questions repeat word for word: desalting and distillation (A3), reforming reactions (A4), delayed coking and FCC (A5), hydrotreating (A6), the amine process (B5), the LNG plant (B6) and separators (B3). Learn the memory tricks and practise each diagram once. The short numericals (API gravity, viscosity blend, VI, porosity, Darcy flow) are easy marks and each has a calculator.

Pass plan

Six papers: 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, a second 2022 set marked “Rejected” in the file (shown here as 2022B; it repeats most 2022 topics, so it is a good extra practice paper) and 2023. Normal papers: 210 marks, answer any THREE of four questions in each section (35 marks each). 2020 was a short exam (120 marks, 1.5 h, any TWO of three per section). Section A is petroleum refining (Shameem sir) and Section B natural gas processing (Muhit sir); in 2021 the sections were swapped (Section A natural gas, Section B refining), so this pack sorts by topic, not question number. Minimum pass set: refining A1-A7 (crude composition, product properties, distillation and desalting, reforming, cracking, hydrotreating and lube, blending numericals) and gas B1-B6 (natural gas and condensate, gas properties, separators, dehydration and hydrates, sweetening, LNG/LPG); B7 (Darcy flow, orifice) is the next to add. In the paper: Section A answer Q1, Q2 and Q3 or Q4; Section B answer Q5, Q6 and Q7 (Q8 if LPG/LNG suits you). Answers follow the teachers’ slides first (Shameem sir: refining; Muhit sir: natural gas L1-L17) and the books they use: Rao Modern Petroleum Refining Processes and Fahim et al. for refining, Sanjay Kumar Gas Production Engineering, Guo & Ghalambor Natural Gas Engineering Handbook and Ahmed for gas. Each answer says where a textbook was used. Every numerical was re-checked in Python.

A1

Crude oil: what it is, composition, classification, impurities, why and how it is refined

Pass set Very likely · 100%Easy

Asked in 6 of 6 papers · 140 marks in total

Study these

  • Crude oil = naturally occurring mixture of hydrocarbons (C 83-87%, H 10-14%) with S, N, O compounds, metals and salts; a fossil fuel formed from buried marine organisms under heat and pressure
  • Hydrocarbon types: paraffins CnH2n+2 (normal and iso), naphthenes CnH2n (rings), aromatics (benzene rings), olefins (made in processing)
  • Classification: paraffinic, naphthenic, aromatic, asphaltic/mixed base; by API (light > 31.1, medium, heavy < 22.3, bitumen < 10); by sulfur (sweet < 0.5%, sour); U.S. Bureau of Mines key fractions; Kw
  • Refining: separation (distillation), conversion (cracking, reforming, alkylation, isomerization), treatment (desalting, hydrotreating), blending

A6

Hydrotreating, hydrogen in the refinery, lube oil processing

Pass set Very likely · 95%Easy

Asked in 5 of 6 papers · 77 marks in total

Study these

  • Hydrotreating: feed + H2 over Co-Mo or Ni-Mo on alumina at 290-400 °C, 10-100 bar; removes S (HDS), N (HDN), O, metals, saturates olefins; H2S removed by amine; protects reformer/FCC catalysts and meets fuel specs
  • Hydrogen sources: catalytic reformer (by-product), steam methane reforming (CH4 + H2O → CO + 3H2, shift CO + H2O → CO2 + H2), partial oxidation, recovery from off-gases
  • Lube oil: vacuum distillation → propane deasphalting → solvent extraction of aromatics (furfural, phenol, NMP) → solvent dewaxing (MEK-toluene) → hydrofinishing → blending with additives
  • Hydrofinishing: mild hydrotreating of the dewaxed base oil to improve colour, odour, oxidation stability

A2

Product properties and test numbers: octane and cetane number, API gravity, flash point, RVP, gasoline grades and pool, diesel classes

Pass set Very likely · 86%Easy

Asked in 5 of 6 papers · 87 marks in total

Study these

  • Octane number = % iso-octane in an iso-octane/n-heptane mix that knocks like the fuel (knock resistance, SI engines); RON (600 rpm, city), MON (900 rpm, highway), sensitivity = RON − MON, PON = (RON + MON)/2
  • Cetane number = % n-cetane in a cetane/α-methylnaphthalene mix with the same ignition delay (CI engines, 40-55 for diesel)
  • API = 141.5/SG − 131.5 (SG at 60 °F); water = 10; flash point = lowest temperature at which vapours flash with a flame; RVP = vapour pressure at 37.8 °C (100 °F) in the Reid bomb
  • Gasoline grades: regular 85-88, mid-grade 88-90, premium > 90; gasoline pool: LSR, isomerate, reformate, FCC, hydrocracked, alkylate, polymer gasoline, n-butane, oxygenates (MTBE, ETBE, TAME, ethanol)

A3

Distillation curves (TBP, ASTM, EFV), desalting, atmospheric and vacuum distillation

Pass set Very likely · 100%Medium

Asked in 6 of 6 papers · 139 marks in total

Study these

  • TBP: batch, 15 theoretical plates, reflux 5 (15/5), atmospheric then 40 mmHg; ASTM D86/D1160: no plates, no reflux (Engler flask), for products; EFV: continuous flash, vapour stays with liquid, for designers; sharpness TBP > ASTM > EFV
  • Desalting: 3-10 vol% wash water + demulsifier, heat to 90-150 °C, electrostatic coalescence (secondary field ~1000 V/cm, primary ~600 V/cm), settling (Stokes); needed if salt > 10 lb/1000 bbl
  • ADU: crude preheated to ~280 °C, furnace to 350-400 °C, 30-50 trays, side strippers, pump-around; products LPG, naphtha, kerosene, diesel/gas oil, atmospheric residue
  • VDU: residue heated to 390-450 °C, 25-40 mmHg flash zone, steam ejectors, packing, wide column; products LVGO, HVGO, lube cuts, vacuum residue

A4

Catalytic reforming and isomerization

Pass set Very likely · 100%Medium

Asked in 6 of 6 papers · 116 marks in total

Study these

  • Reforming upgrades heavy naphtha (RON 50-60) to reformate (RON 90-105), makes aromatics and H2; Pt (0.2-0.6%) on chlorided alumina, bifunctional (metal: dehydrogenation; acid: isomerization, cyclization)
  • Reactions: dehydrogenation of naphthenes (fast, very endothermic), dehydroisomerization of alkylcyclopentanes, dehydrocyclization of paraffins (slow), isomerization (mild exothermic), hydrocracking (slow, exothermic, unwanted)
  • SR (semi-regenerative): 3-4 fixed beds with interheaters, 12-15 bar, regenerated every 6-24 months; CCR: moving bed, 3-10 bar, continuous regeneration, Pt-Sn, RON 98-105+
  • Isomerization: n-C5/n-C6 → branched isomers at 95-205 °C, Pt/chlorided alumina or zeolite; raises RON by 12-20; catalyst poisons: S, N, water, metals, coke

A5

Cracking and coking: thermal cracking, hydrocracking, delayed and fluid coking, visbreaking, FCC

Pass set Very likely · 86%Medium

Asked in 4 of 6 papers · 97 marks in total

Study these

  • Thermal cracking: heat (450-750 °C) and pressure break large molecules, free radical, no catalyst; hydrocracking: catalytic cracking + hydrogenation at high H2 pressure, bifunctional catalyst, saturated, sulfur-free products
  • Delayed coking: residue heated to ~500 °C in a furnace, cracks in large coke drums (two drums, switched every ~24 h); vapours to fractionator; coke cut out by water jets (2000-4500 psig)
  • Visbreaking: mild thermal cracking of vacuum residue to cut viscosity and pour point; coil (474-500 °C in the furnace, quench at exit) vs soaker (427-438 °C, extra time in a soaking drum)
  • FCC: hot catalyst (zeolite) meets feed in the riser (480-540 °C), cracks in seconds; spent (coked) catalyst steam-stripped and regenerated by burning coke (650-815 °C); heat balance

A7

Product blending: objectives, blending indices (RVP, viscosity, flash point), viscosity index numericals

Pass set Likely · 77%Medium

Asked in 4 of 6 papers · 77 marks in total

Study these

  • Objective: combine semi-finished streams to meet product specifications at the lowest cost and maximum profit
  • Linear (additive) properties: SG, sulfur, boiling point: Pblend = ΣxiPi; non-linear ones use blending indices: RVP BI = RVP1.25
  • Viscosity: BI = logν/(3 + logν); BIblend = Σxv,iBIi; νblend = 103BI/(1−BI)
  • Viscosity index VI = 100(L − U)/(L − H): U = oil’s viscosity at 40 °C, L and H = 40 °C viscosities of VI 0 and VI 100 reference oils with the same 100 °C viscosity

B5

Gas sweetening: reasons for removing H2S and CO2, amine process, iron sponge, molecular sieve, sulfur recovery

Pass set Very likely · 95%Easy

Asked in 5 of 6 papers · 70 marks in total

Study these

  • Acid gases: H2S (toxic, fatal above 600 ppm, corrosive, burns to SO2, poisons catalysts); CO2 (no heating value, carbonic acid corrosion, freezes in LNG plants); both promote hydrates
  • Amine (MEA, DEA, MDEA): lean amine absorbs acid gas in a contactor (counter-current, ~38 °C, high P); rich amine flashed, heated, stripped in a regenerator (~115-125 °C, low P) and recycled
  • Iron sponge: Fe2O3 on wood chips: Fe2O3 + 3H2S → Fe2S3 + 3H2O; batch, for < 300 ppm H2S, does not remove CO2; regenerated with air: 2Fe2S3 + 3O2 → 2Fe2O3 + 6S
  • Claus: H2S + 1.5O2 → SO2 + H2O; 2H2S + SO2 → 3S + 2H2O
  1. 2023Q8(a)12 marks

B6

LNG and LPG: LNG plant and refrigeration cycles, storage and carriers, LPG uses and hazards, LPG vs LNG vs CNG, NGL recovery

Pass set Very likely · 100%Medium

Asked in 6 of 6 papers · 202 marks in total

Study these

  • LNG: natural gas cooled to −162 °C at ~1 atm, 1/600 of gas volume; plant: inlet separation → acid gas removal → dehydration → mercury removal → NGL recovery → liquefaction (cascade, mixed refrigerant, C3-MR, expander) → N2 rejection → storage
  • Cascade: propane (−35 °C), ethylene (−100 °C), methane (−160 °C) cycles; each refrigerant has a limited range, so three are needed to span ambient to −162 °C with small temperature approach
  • LPG: propane/butane mix (Bangladesh ~30/70), liquid at 4-15 bar, heavier than air, odorized; uses domestic, commercial, industrial, autogas, refrigerant, feedstock; hazards: leaks, fire/BLEVE, asphyxiation, cold burns
  • LNG carriers: double hull, Moss spherical or membrane tanks (9% Ni steel, aluminium, Invar), insulation, boil-off used as fuel

B1

Natural gas: what it is, origin, classification, condensate, reservoirs, Bangladesh outlook

Pass set Very likely · 100%Medium

Asked in 6 of 6 papers · 166 marks in total

Study these

  • Natural gas: mixture of light hydrocarbons, mainly methane, with ethane, propane, butanes and N2, CO2, H2S, He; colourless, odourless, lighter than air
  • Origin: thermogenic (organic matter buried, heated and compressed: kerogen → oil → gas), biogenic (methanogenic bacteria at shallow depth), abiogenic (deep inorganic, minor theory); traps under cap rock
  • Classification: associated (with oil) vs non-associated; dry (lean) vs wet (rich in C2+); sweet vs sour; conventional vs unconventional (shale gas, tight gas, coal-bed methane, hydrates)
  • Condensate: C5+ liquids that drop out when the gas cools below its hydrocarbon dew point; separated in field separators, stabilized, split into naphtha, kerosene, diesel; retrograde condensation in the reservoir

B3

Gas-liquid separators: vertical, horizontal, double-barrel, spherical, three-phase; internals; sizing

Pass set Very likely · 100%Medium

Asked in 6 of 6 papers · 135 marks in total

Study these

  • Separation by momentum change (inlet diverter), gravity settling, coalescence (mist extractor); sections: primary (inlet), gravity settling, liquid collection, mist extractor
  • Vertical: handles slugs and sand, small footprint, larger/costlier; horizontal: smaller and cheaper for high gas-oil ratio, larger interface, poor with solids and surges; double-barrel: liquid drains to lower barrel, no re-entrainment; spherical: compact, cheap, limited surge
  • Internals: inlet diverter (baffle or centrifugal), wave breakers, defoaming plates, vortex breaker, mist extractor (wire mesh, vanes), level and pressure controllers
  • Sizing (Souders-Brown): D2 = qgZ(T + 460)ρg0.5/[2.40Kp(ρL − ρg)0.5]; liquid VL = Wt/1440; L/D 3-8

B4

Water in natural gas: dehydration, water content (Campbell), hydrates

Pass set Very likely · 100%Medium

Asked in 6 of 6 papers · 122 marks in total

Study these

  • Why dehydrate: free water forms hydrates (plugging), causes corrosion with CO2/H2S, slugging, lower heating value; pipeline limit 6-8 lb/MMscf
  • Water content falls with pressure, rises with temperature, falls with salinity and gas gravity; Campbell: W = yHCWHC + yCO2WCO2 + yH2SWH2S from three charts
  • Hydrates: ice-like crystals of water cages holding gas molecules (CH4, C2H6, C3H8, CO2, H2S); need free water, low T, high P, agitation; prevented by dehydration, heating, pressure reduction, methanol/glycol injection, kinetic and anti-agglomerant inhibitors
  • Dehydration: absorption by glycol (TEG contactor + reboiler at 175-205 °C) or adsorption on solid desiccants (alumina, silica gel, molecular sieves: two towers, adsorb/regenerate)

B2

Gas properties and rock properties: z-factor, pseudo-reduced properties, density, Bg, compressibility, viscosity, porosity and permeability

Pass set Very likely · 95%Hard

Asked in 5 of 6 papers · 85 marks in total

Study these

  • Real gas: pV = znRT; z from the Standing-Katz chart at ppr = p/ppc, Tpr = T/Tpc; Kay’s rule ppc = Σyipci, Tpc = ΣyiTci; Wichert-Aziz correction for CO2, H2S
  • ρg = pMa/(zRT), R = 10.73 psia ft3/(lb-mol °R); Bg = 0.02827zT/p ft3/scf; cg = 1/p − (1/z)(∂z/∂p)T
  • Viscosity by Carr-Kobayashi-Burrows: μ1 at 1 atm from M or γg and T, plus N2, CO2, H2S corrections
  • Porosity φ = pore volume/bulk volume (storage); permeability k = ability to transmit fluid (darcy, Darcy’s law)

B7

Reservoir flow and gas measurement: Darcy’s law (linear and radial), orifice meter, choosing a meter

Next to add Likely · 73%Medium

Asked in 3 of 6 papers · 67 marks in total

Study these

  • Darcy (field units, linear): q = 0.001127kA(p1 − p2)/(μL) bbl/day with k in md, A ft2, p psi, μ cp, L ft; apparent velocity v = q/A, actual (interstitial) velocity = v/φ
  • Radial steady state: p = pwf + [QoBoμo/(0.00708kh)]ln(r/rw); most pressure drop is near the well
  • Flow regimes: steady, unsteady (transient), pseudo-steady; geometries: radial, linear, spherical/hemispherical; fluids: incompressible, slightly compressible, compressible
  • Orifice meter: thin plate with a hole; Δp across it gives flow by Bernoulli: q = CAo√(2Δp/ρ); AGA-3 for gas; selection by accuracy, range, pressure loss, cost, fluid cleanliness
